# JDM VG33E Engine Swap

> **[Unverified]** This page rests on a single community report. Cross-check before relying on it.

> Items marked **[Partial]** are only partly confirmed by the source and need more work. They stay in the review queue and are firmed up, corrected or removed as more sources come in.

## Summary

[Partial] Swap out or relocate the knock sensor and replace accessory brackets to match the new JDM VG33E engine. [t1094]

## Procedure

> **[Partial]** Needs more work: the verifier could confirm only part of this procedure (the steps marked [Partial], or whether the list is complete). Steps or precautions may be wrong or missing; read the source thread before relying on it. Later runs fill it in as more sources are found.

1. Remove the rear engine coolant lines (two hard lines) and swap them to match the new intake.
2. [Partial] Swap out or relocate the knock sensor if access is difficult, though swapping may suffice.
3. [Partial] Replace the accessory brackets on the JDM block with those from the original vehicle.
4. [Partial] Install a new upper intake manifold gasket and fit the top intake plenum.
5. [Partial] Check the harmonic balancer; swap it out only if not identical to the donor engine's version.
6. [Partial] Swap the transmission output: install an MT flywheel or Auto flex plate as needed, including bushings/pilot bearings.

_Procedure reported by [t1094]._

## Parts

- [Partial] JDM VG33E Engine: Often found with 45K-70K miles [t1094]
- [Partial] Upper Intake Manifold Gasket [t1094]

## Tips & gotchas

- Perform the swap with the engine outside the bay for easier access. [t1094]
- Utilize the original wiring harness if swapping the intake manifold, as connectors may not need modification. [t1094]
